messages:
alex_h: Heads-up — scheduling a maintenance window for the theta-gpu pool tomorrow 03:00-05:00 UTC. Plan is rolling reboots (2 nodes at a time) to apply PCIe firmware + microkernel patch. Expected transient capacity drop ~8-12% for bursty tenants. Full plan below.

maya_r: Is 03:00 the lowest traffic for EU? worried about shift-based loads.

alex_h: Per telemetry, global p50 is fine at 03:00, EU has a spike around 05:30 UTC so we stop before then. That was intentional.

tj_ops: Can we pre-warm major prefix caches and run a lightweight KV seed 20-30m before drain to reduce cold starts?

alex_h: Yes — recommend running the seed job 30m prior. Command I ran in staging:```bash
./tools/prefix-seed --pool theta-gpu --shards 8 --rate 200
```
This runs ~10m and keeps top prefixes in memory.

ops-bot: [incident-bot] Scheduled maintenance created: theta-gpu pool. Start=2026-03-21T03:00:00Z End=2026-03-21T05:00:00Z Rolling=2-per-cohort. Notifying affected tenants.

lucy_sre: Oncall checklist: set alert if model-generation p99 latency >200ms for 10m or error-rate increase >0.8%. If triggered, abort further drains and revert cohort. I'll attach thresholds to the runbook.

samir_p: Budget question — will Dedicated customers incur capacity coverage charges? We should mark this as "platform maintenance" so cost center covers burst. Ops finance: allocation rule is 1.5x short-window hedge.

alex_h: Good point. I've flagged finance. Also: we'll mark two canary nodes per AZ to validate driver before broad rollout. Canary steps:```yaml
- drain node canary-1
- reboot with firmware v1.4.3
- run smoke: ./smoke/gpu-health.sh --samples 20
- check p99 latency, memory errors, PCIe errors in dmesg
```
If smoke fails we automatically halt.

maya_r: What's fallback if a cohort fails? do we have a soft-fallback to older driver image?

tj_ops: Yes — runtime supports running older driver variant (driver-legacy) and we can route traffic there via pool-tag routing for affected tenants for up to 2 hours while we investigate. That will increase tail latency ~30-40ms.

alex_h: Network note — one of the reboots touches NIC firmware on the racked hosts. We will stagger NIC flashes so control-plane BGP adjacencies don't all flap at once. Sequence: flash NIC on isolation rack A -> verify egress metrics 5m -> continue.

lucy_sre: Ops to run synthetic validator against o11y endpoints after each cohort: `curl -sS https://o11y.prod.redwood/ping | jq .latency` — if >250ms, roll cohort back.

ops-bot: Reminder: tenant-notice email will go out at T-12h and T-1h. Channel updates in #cust-comm will be posted automatically.

samir_p: Please add expected cost delta to the maintenance ticket. Rough estimate: 1.5x burst for 2 hours on 20% of pool = ~0.3% monthly spend bump for March.

alex_h: I'll post the runbook link and the maintenance ticket shortly: https://redwood.internal/ops/maint/8250012345 (runbook attached there).

maya_r: Ack. I'll coordinate EU oncall overlap and keep PMs notifed.

lucy_sre: Oncall will be monitoring from 02:45-06:00 UTC. Pager duty rotation updated.

alex_h: Final ask — if you own any scheduled heavy training jobs, please drain them or reschedule. Use `kubectl label job <name> no-maint=true` to opt-out during window.

tj_ops: Adding last perf note: after reboot we must re-seed L0 caches for model sampler to avoid token regen spikes. I'll bake that into the post-rollout checklist.

alex_h: Thanks all — we'll proceed unless any block by EOD. :thumbsup:
